findings.title: Inside Coruna and DarkSword Chains: From Web Lures to iOS Exploitation
findings.summary_md: Zimperium zLabs identified 608 domains delivering Coruna-family exploit code through October 2026, with recovered configurations across 93 sites mapping to 21 distinct tracking collectors. The infrastructure serves two OS-conditioned chains: the legacy Coruna framework for iOS 17.2.1 and earlier, and a DarkSword-derived chain for iOS 18.4 to 18.7, delivered via hidden iframes on lure and compromised sites. The report documents native modules with kernel memory read and write routines, AMFI state manipulation, encrypted command-and-control traffic, and cleanup routines that delete crash logs and Safari website data.

findings.title: The Proliferation of DarkSword: iOS Exploit Chain Adopted by Multiple Threat Actors
findings.summary_md: Google Threat Intelligence Group disclosed DarkSword on March 18, 2026 as a full-chain iOS exploit used by multiple actors since at least November 2025, targeting iOS 18.4 to 18.7 via compromised legitimate websites. The chain uses six vulnerabilities, several originally exploited as zero-days, and has been adopted by commercial surveillance vendors and suspected state actors including UNC6353, a suspected Russian espionage cluster that added it to watering-hole attacks on Ukrainian sites. Apple patched all of the flaws by iOS 26.3.
